title: From physics to products
summary: The Work Passport begins in August 2017, after the PhD chapter. A transition into industry led to the Physics Project Manager role at Hawkes Learning (November 2017–January 2018), coordinating physics courseware development. August is the archive boundary, not a claimed employment start date.

title: Antennas, arrays & leadership
summary: Joined Northrop Grumman in Baltimore in January 2018. Early assignments included algorithm development for an internal computational electromagnetics toolkit and installed-performance analysis for SEWIP. RAPTR followed as a scalable radar product-line offering aimed at Army Future Vertical Lift and drone radar applications; additive-manufactured antenna development primarily supported the company's proposed Navy Future X-Band Radar (FXR) offering. Later responsibilities included leadership of a 16-person engineering group.

title: Systems at mission scale
summary: My September 2021 move from Baltimore to Boulder was a management-level advancement, from Manager 2 to Manager 3 (roughly manager to senior manager depending on the organization). It also required three significant adjustments: moving from a large site to a smaller site, transitioning from leadership of a small team to a much larger and geographically dispersed organization, and moving from radar subject-matter expertise into systems engineering for space-to-ground communications. The distributed leadership challenge was the biggest. RGS-A was my first major space-to-ground communications assignment after the move. Boulder has remained my Northrop Grumman career base since September 2021. As Systems Engineering Manager 3, I eventually oversaw approximately 50 engineers across four managers supporting OPIR ground processing. On November 15, 2025, I became Senior Staff Chief Engineer, continuing to work on space and ground systems without a separate Aurora career-base move.
